recipes.name: My Crab Cakes
ingredients_raw: 1 cup panko (Japanese bread crumbs) or regular dry bread crumbs
0.5 cup olive oil, or as needed

steps.text: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over high heat. Sauté green onions in hot oil until tender; set aside to cool slightly.

Combine crabmeat, sautéed green onions, crushed crackers, egg, mayonnaise, dry mustard, garlic powder, cayenne pepper, garlic powder, Old Bay seasoning, salt, and pepper. Form into ten 1/2-inch-thick patties.
Place bread crumbs in a shallow bowl. Press patties in bread crumbs to coat.
Heat 1/2 cup olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook patties in hot oil until golden brown on each side. Drain briefly on a paper towel-lined plate and serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: My Crab Cakes
raw_recipe.description: This crab cake recipe features canned crabmeat with green onion, egg, mayo, Old Bay, and crackers coated in bread crumbs, then pan-fried until golden.

review.reviewBody: Yumm. I have made these crabcakes many times and I have made some changes to the recipe that I think work better. In ingredients I used 2 6oz. cans crabmeat, 2 eggs, 6 oz. (approx. 20) ritz crackers, and 1/2 tsp. Old Bay seasonings, and only 1/2 cup breadcrumbs. Everything else I kept the same. I did not saute my green onions in oil, but followed the rest of the recipe the same. I would reduce the amount of oil in pan for frying. I serve with aioli. This is the best recipe I've found: 3/4 cup mayo, 3 cloves minced garlic, 2 1/2 tbsp. lemon juice, 3/4 tsp. salt and 1/2 tsp. pepper. Stir all together, and chill. GREAT!!!

These are turning into one of our favorites! I've made them a number of times and have done some tweaking to the recipe. I use just one sleeve of reduced-fat Town House crackers, and I combine them with the green onions, black pepper, and some garlic powder in the food processor. I use two 6-ounce cans of crabmeat, and one tablespoon of Dijon mustard instead of the dry mustard. 

Also, I use reduced-fat mayo, and I always put in double the cayenne, as well as fresh pressed garlic instead of the garlic powder. I then coat them with cornmeal and bake them in a 350 oven for 20 minutes, or until they're warmed through - a lower-fat alternative to frying. Thanks for sharing!

These were good; however, I had a difficult time with their holding together. I may have had more crab meat than that called for. I ended up adding a bit more mayonnaise to help it stick together. Also, as one reviewer suggested, it helped to chill them before putting them in the oil to fry. I just popped them I. The freezer for about 10 minutes or so. They handled much better.

I've seen this variation before many times. Being a foodie, I'm willing to give anything the benefit of a doubt. In S.C. they use green pepper and onion. I've had those too. I used a can of salmon because I grew up eating them (crab cakes) differently. Mom Mom would use minimal filler, seafood seasoning, and a binder. Of course, leftover crab meat from the steamed crabs we recently had was the source. Traditions are great. No one ever bought crab meat back then. There are just too many changes required to this recipe for my taste. So if you want to make the easiest Md style cakes read on. Do yourself a favor. Buy fresh crabmeat if possible. Or buy the best canned lump or jumbo lump available to you. One pound. If you buy canned, and it contains a lot of moisture, let some drain, but save it. Get some Hellmann's Mayo. You need a half cup. McCormick & Co. makes a "Crab Cake" seasoning pack, look it up. Gently mix the seasoning pack with the crabmeat, and then gently fold in the mayo. Shape the mix into no more than 4 cakes, 3" dia. Fry in a pan, little to no oil, just a touch of cooking spray if anything, on med, med/high, 3 min flip, 3 min done. Don't burn them! Serve with any mustard mixed with as much of the reserved crabmeat liquid as you want (this is my spin) on the side and just a couple saltines. Careful, a dab of mustard goes a long way. Open a National Bohemian aka Natty Bo and your in early 1900s Baltimore City. Guaranteed. I do appreciate trying new recipes but this one failed for me. Sorry. Try mine.

Way too many breadcrumbs in this recipe. Next time I make this, I will knock it down at least 20%. The "salt and pepper to taste" is a cop out. I added a teaspoon, but it should have been more (please stop doing this in your recipes, give people a clue at least). 1/4 teaspoon Old Bay was weak - it needed at least 1/2 if not a full teaspoon. And the Panko crumbs don't stick. I gave my patties a milk-butter-egg bath before dipping them in crumb to give them a much better coating.

I made these crab cakes for the Super Bowl. I ramped the recipe up to 18 servings so that 8 people would each get at least 2, and a couple of extras. I felt that that the mixture was loose and a little bland after the adjusted amounts were given. I altered the recipe by adding an extra egg (3), and instead of the Old Bay, I added crab seasoning and left the salt out. When the crab cake were done, I finished them with the crab cake seasoning and served them with a wasabi/ mayonnaise/ mixture with lemon juice. They were good and I would make this recipe again with my own adjustments. Thanks for the recipe!

I was craving crab cakes, and this recipe was perfect! I made a few adjustments based on what I could find at the store. I used two 6 oz cans of crabmeat, 20 ritz crackers that I crushed in the food processor, I didn’t sauté the green onions, I put the mix in the freezer for a half hour before I formed the patties, and I dipped the patties in egg before the panko. I made four cakes. I will be making these again...possibly today

I have made this many times and freeze the cakes for a quick evening meal. Because we have them kinda regularly, and crab meat can be costly, for 4 cakes, I substitute 1 ea package imitation crab shredded and aprrox. 20 ea medium shrimp cooked and diced. We always use Ritz crackers.

Added 2 x 120 gr crab meat (weight is drained crabmeat from tin), teaspoon more mayo, chopped green onion without frying 1st. No need for extra panko. Delicious and probably one of the better recipes for crab cakes. Next time I'll add another tin of crab meat.

I tweaked it quite a bit based on review so my rating is based on the changes. I used 1 package fresh imitation crab meat, 2 eggs, 1/2 cup mayo, 1 tbsp dijon mustard, and 6 ounces Ritz crackers, which is a lot, 8 ozs would have been way too much. I baked them in the oven at 350 for 30 mins flipping halfway through. they came out great this way

I served it with the recommended aioli on here - 3/4 cup mayo, 3 cloves crushed garlic, 2 1/2 tbsp lemon juice, salt & pepper to taste

Great! The only things I changed were to not saute the green onions (I like them a little crunchy) and doubled the garlic (personal taste). It was my first try at making crab cakes, so it was a perfect intro/base recipe.

This was by far the best crab cakes I've made. Coating them in the breadcrumbs makes a huge difference! Fairly simple also. They even held up as leftovers, too. My only edits were: I didn't have butter style crackers, so I used about half and half club crackers and garlic pita crackers and pulsed them in the food processor.
Good, except I got only 6- 2 3/4' x 3/4 thick patties. (Bun sized) If 10 were made, they'd be quite small.
Easy to assemble and very tasty- I used GF panko breadcrumbs but in a recipe like this with lots of flavor no one can tell the difference and I got lots of accolades
I followed the recipe exactly and we really enjoyed these. They are delicate before they are cooked so getting them into the pan and flipping them takes skill.
The worst I've ever tried! A great big waste of money and time like trying one of ree drummonds recipes!
Taste and easy directions
This was easy to follow. I definitely will make it again.
Came out great! I deleted the dry mustard and added a couple teaspoons of warshyoursister sauce
Perfect recipe. I will use a bit less cayenne pepper. It was a bit too strong for a couple of family members.
